body:
- Email campaign performance check-in — A recent summer email went out and is generating results. At least two people responded requesting OS demos, including one who asked about billing capabilities (which confirmed the product has it). The team noted the responses weren't directly tied to the email content, which sparked a conversation about what that signals.

- Email segmentation discussion — They reviewed a send that targeted people who had opened but not clicked. The team found it counterintuitive — you'd expect the more engaged clickers to convert — but the responses came from that segment anyway. General read: it's working, people are clicking, that's what matters.

- "Hotel Weekly Program Template" lead magnet — An email asset (apparently a hotel workout template) drove at least one demo request. One person on the call seemed surprised it existed ("I didn't know we were doing that"). Confirmed it's generating clicks and interest.

- A/B test idea floated — Concept of testing a CTA-to-demo version vs. a free downloadable version of email campaigns to see which converts better.

- StoryBuildr beta is ready — The tool is built but untested. Plan is to test it, film a Loom walkthrough, and send to the team (and James). The main technical challenge discussed: Facebook/Instagram don't allow scraping, so Firecrawl was recommended as a workaround to pull limited post metadata (top 3–4 posts, captions, content type). Email audit functionality will likely be generic/survey-based since API access to MailChimp isn't realistic. Core value framed as story harvesting — auditing current content is a nice-to-have.

- Outreach platform decision — Instantly — Team appears to have settled on Instantly over Apollo (deemed too enterprise) and Ocean.io (unknown). Decision driven by the fact they're already using it and the existing contact database. Someone is emailing Eric to confirm and see if a meeting is still needed.

Mark Fisher outreach — Team discussed reaching out to Mark Fisher (who attends Perform Better conferences and has a relationship with Pete Dupuy from Cressy). One person offered to fire off an email to see if he's interested in something.

Perform Better conference — Reviewed upcoming dates: Long Beach July 9, Providence/Rhode Island August 20. No strong appetite to attend on short notice. Flagged as a "back of mind" item for future planning.

Spagnola follow-up — Came up briefly, sounds like he never confirmed. Team wrote it off.
Ken confirmed as a collaborator/partner — Replied positively ("I love it, let me know what you need from me"). Next step is to map out exactly what they want from him.

Kind of feels like we're at a decision point of sorts for OS. Do we invest in smoothing out the onboarding/operational side of things with SSO or do we focus on more "tactical" updates like pricing page links, member timeline, or reporting enhancement.

Ideas that Trent presented at the start: 
- SSO to smooth out member onboarding/profile set up
- individual links for each pricing option on the member-facing web app
- Member Timeline/History
- Revisit the Churn/At-Risk report update

Or do we start to talk about integrating AI functionality into OS? This feels like it's a bit cart-before-the-horse, but worth a short discussion.
- is this something that allows us to increase ACV by adding another subscription level

Focus on features that have demand based on feedback for 2026, shift to future-facing projects in 2027

Settled on revisiting Churn/At-Risk reporting and maybe a small overhaul of the General Reporting page. Goal would be to strip down the project to it's studs and set us up for a simpler implementation that doesn't involve tying Packages into the Churn report.

body:
Scheduling booking window — Someone has nearly filled their 90-day booking window slots, which was the main goal; acknowledged it's tedious but important work

Client scheduling complexity (Jeff) 
— Discussed a specific customer (Jeff) whose schedule is complex — rentable bays (golf sims), regular strength sessions, and open gym — and the current schedule builder isn't well-suited for that use case

Member-booked appointments feature — This upcoming feature was identified as the likely fix for Jeff's situation; kick-off is next week with an expected mid-August completion. The recommendation was to bridge the gap for 6–7 weeks and potentially offer a temporary discount if he pushes back

Schedule copy functionality — Discussed adding the ability to copy a session within a day and across a week; noted both would be needed together and flagged the UX risk of giving users too many options to edit simultaneously, which could cause confusion or mistakes

Onboarding customer audit — Trent wants to kick off a structured customer interview process to learn what went wrong during onboarding; emphasized keeping it focused (not a feature wishlist or complaint session); plan is to vet the process first with Andrea, then move to Brie

AI-powered onboarding blueprint tool — Trent demoed/discussed a Claude Project ("Onboarding Assistant") that would take a pre-sales intake call transcript and generate a tailored OS setup blueprint for the customer — covering categories, classes, appointments, memberships, staff permissions, and studio settings

OS schema review — Walked through what the Onboarding Assistant currently knows about OS (categories, schedule item types, products, staff profiles, studio settings) and solicited feedback on gaps

Membership setup UX improvements — Discussed adding tooltip/info callout icons (ⓘ) next to fields like "payment due date" and "membership start date" to reduce confusion; flagged common setup mistakes like collapsing everything into one category or failing to assign multiple categories to a membership; framed as a fast-twitch build since it's just on-hover copy with no logic changes
